questions.q: How late did the captain expect the Rangoon to be because of the storm?
choices: Two days, or perhaps three
Twenty hours, or more if the storm lasted
Only a few hours at the very most
A whole week, since the engine was broken
questions.evidence: she would reach Hong Kong twenty hours behind time

questions.q: How did Mr. Fogg react to the storm that might cost him the wager?
choices: He paced the deck and complained to the captain
He stayed calm, as if it were planned
He shut himself in his cabin and would not come out
He offered the crew money to sail faster through it
questions.evidence: it seemed as if the storm were a part of his programme

questions.q: Why was Fix pleased by the storm, even though it made him sea-sick?
choices: Each delay made it likelier Fogg would be stuck in Hong Kong
He enjoyed rough weather at sea and liked to stand and watch the big waves
He hoped Passepartout would fall overboard in the gale
It gave him time to read his letters from London
questions.evidence: Each delay filled him with hope

questions.q: What did Passepartout do to the barometer?
choices: He broke it
He shook it
He hid it
He fixed it
questions.evidence: Passepartout shook it, but with no perceptible effect

questions.q: "Passepartout was enraged beyond expression by the unpropitious weather." What does "unpropitious" mean?
choices: Warm and sunny
Unlucky
Cold and snowy
Quiet and still
questions.evidence: Passepartout was enraged beyond expression by the unpropitious weather

questions.q: Why had the Carnatic not left Hong Kong for Yokohama on time?
choices: One of her boilers had to be repaired
Her captain was sick in the hospital
She was waiting for the mail from India
The storm had kept her in the harbour
questions.evidence: they had to repair one of her boilers

questions.q: How did Passepartout show his joy at the pilot's news?
choices: He danced a jig on the deck of the Rangoon
He shook the pilot's hand and called him the best of good fellows
He ran straight down to the saloon to tell Aouda and Fix the good news at once
He gave the pilot all the money he had in his pockets
questions.evidence: Pilot, you are the best of good fellows!

questions.q: Why was being a day late to Yokohama not a serious problem for Fogg?
choices: The Pacific steamer waited for the Hong Kong boat, and the time could be made up
Fogg had planned for a whole extra week in Japan from the very start
The bet allowed him to be late at any one stop along the route
The captain of the Carnatic promised to sail twice as fast as usual
questions.evidence: it could not sail until the latter reached Yokohama

questions.q: What did Fogg learn about Aouda's cousin Jeejeeh?
choices: He had died the year before in Hong Kong
He had moved to Europe, probably Holland, two years before
He had gone to Bombay to look for Aouda
He was away on business in Japan and would not be back for at least a month
questions.evidence: Jeejeeh had left China two years before

questions.q: What did Fogg tell Passepartout to do after Aouda agreed to go on to Europe?
choices: Find her a safe hotel in Hong Kong
Engage three cabins on the Carnatic
Send a telegram to Holland at once
Buy her new trunks and warm clothes
questions.evidence: Go to the Carnatic, and engage three cabins.

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: A storm delays the ship, but Fogg can still catch the Carnatic, and Aouda joins the trip
Fix arrests Fogg as soon as the Rangoon lands at the quay in Hong Kong
Passepartout gets lost in the streets of Hong Kong and misses the boat
Aouda finds her cousin and decides to stay in Hong Kong for good
